methods.name: Peer-Median

data.narrative:
INERATEC is a Series B-stage climate and energy technology company founded by Tim Boeltken that has raised $129M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of nine private companies and one public comparable (LNZA) operating in the same sector, including later-stage peers such as KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Amogy.

Two valuation methods were applied. The stage-progression approach uses the $129M in total capital raised as a proxy for current value and applies a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B-to-next-stage advancement, implying a valuation of $245M. The peer-median method triangulates across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—KoBold Metals ($3.0B, Series C), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B, Series C), and Amogy ($700M, Series C)—yielding a median valuation of $1.0B, with a range of $700M to $3.0B.

The triangulated analysis across both methods supports a valuation range of $208M to $1.1B, with a median of $623M. The wide dispersion reflects meaningful uncertainty around stage-adjusted peer multiples in the climate-tech sector, where later-stage funding rounds have shown considerable variance. Key uncertainties include the relative maturity and capital intensity of INERATEC's technology relative to the Series C peers used for comparison, and whether the stage-progression multiplier adequately reflects current market conditions for Series B climate companies.
